title: Weight codes, scales and reconstruction
description: Distinguish grouped weight storage, reconstruction error and the model behavior measured after loading.

terms.definition: Represent learned weights with integer codes and scales. This chapter saves four-bit codes and reconstructs f64 weights before using the existing model; quantization performs no retraining.
Consecutive weights within one matrix row that share a scale. The chosen group size is a maximum count; a shorter final group keeps its own scale, and groups never cross rows.
The largest absolute weight in a group divided by seven in this representation. An all-zero group instead uses scale one. Smaller scales give more closely spaced reconstructed levels.
An integer from minus seven through seven whose reconstructed weight is the code times its group scale. Zero point is zero; the four-bit code minus eight is reserved and rejected.
Restrict a rounded code to the permitted endpoints. A fixed scale can clip weights outside its range; the ideal half-scale rounding-error bound applies only without clipping.
Store two four-bit codes in one byte, first code in the low nibble and second in the high nibble. An odd matrix weight count leaves the final high nibble zero and unused.
Reconstruct each weight by multiplying its signed code by the corresponding row-group scale. The loader returns ordinary f64 matrices and preserves the text embedding and output head's shared table.

The difference between a reconstructed value and its source. Maximum absolute error and mean squared error describe different aspects; a weight-error summary alone does not determine a layer's product error or a model's likelihood.

The stored tensor data, including code bytes, scales, logical shapes and unchanged tensors or assets. A complete SafeTensors file also includes header and configuration bytes, so code bytes alone do not measure file size.
